title: Choose the visual world for Batch
question: The roll assigned Technique Plate. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Technique Plate
options.lineage: Swiss instructional charts and pastry-school technique plates — International Typographic Style put to work
options.thesis: Every recipe is a numbered plate on chart paper; the tree is the chart's construction grid made visible.
materials: black ink rules — hairline and heavy
options.viewport: Top rail: white, heavy black rule beneath, 'Batch' wordmark + a 2×2 grid mark with one blue cell (a base with one component changed); nav as numbered plates 01 Tree · 02 Recipes · 03 Queue · 04 Mix-ins. Below: full-bleed chart paper with a faint square grid. Recipes are plates — white rectangles, hairline black frame, heavy black head rule carrying the kicker (BASE / VARIANT / SUB-RECIPE) — name in heavy grotesk, macros in tabular numerals. Edges route orthogonally at 45/90°, interchange rings where a sub-recipe joins. Controls sit in the corners; the center is the graph. Bake card: title in heavy grotesk, a solid blue spec block with white numerals (kcal · protein · cal/g · makes), ingredients as a ruled table, steps as large gutter numerals, notes as marked marginalia (▲ pitfall ◆ technique ● note).
options.risk: Reads cold if the grid is rigid and the type timid — the plate must earn poster scale (large numerals, heavy rules) or it collapses into a spreadsheet.

raised.raise: Edges bend only at 45° and 90° with interchange rings at every composition join; hovering a plate traces its whole route — ancestors and sub-recipes light, the rest dims.
State is a mark, not a hue: ○ to-make, ● tried, ★ excellent, ▲ over the lean line. Blue never means status — only structure and selection.
Every zone carries its literal label plate (INGREDIENTS · METHOD · MAKE NEXT); wayfinding is reading, never icon-guessing.
Canvas controls pinned to the safe-area corners at every width; the center stays empty for the graph.
One dominant field per phone viewport: the tree becomes an outline-first page on phones; the canvas is a step away, never an overlay covering controls.
Back retraces the exact trail: undo/redo stays, and the modal names the plate you came from.

options.label: Formula Sheet
options.lineage: the professional bakery's production formula sheet — baker's percentages on a ruled grid
options.thesis: Every recipe is a production formula: quantities, ratios, and macros in one ruled grid you can run a shift from.
options.viewport: The tree as a ruled production schedule: bases as bold header rows, variants indented beneath, sub-recipes as call-outs in the margin; macros and the ratio as the rightmost ledger columns; the queue as a shift list with highlighter on what's next.
options.risk: Familiar — a spreadsheet-like data UI is where most runs in this category land; the graph loses its shape as a graph.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: metropolitan rail map fired as a midnight-blue enamel mural
options.thesis: Lineage as lines: each base is a line, variants are stations, sub-recipes are interchanges, and the chosen recipe's route burns brightest.
options.viewport: The tree as a transit diagram on enamel: lines bending at 45/90°, station dots per recipe, interchange rings where sub-recipes join; a route search at top; the bake card slides in as a station board.
options.case: Fused, it wins audience identification — a graph the builder reads daily — and loses clarity on the bake card and the 92-row index: dark enamel is the wrong reading ground under kitchen light with floury hands.
options.risk: A dark surface read on a phone in a bright kitchen; four line colors invent a hierarchy the recipes don't have.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.lineage: film cutting bench flattened into a sheet
options.thesis: Recipes as frames on a perforated rail; where you stopped is a folded flag.
options.viewport: A perforated rail crossing every page at a fixed height; the queue as frames strung between pins.
options.case: Loses both axes: a baker does not identify with the cutting room, and one condensed size in orange-on-black cannot carry a 92-row macro table.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.lineage: industrial streetwear — quoted labels, zip ties, hazard stripes
options.thesis: Every zone named in straight quotes; the hazard stripe runs under what matters.
options.viewport: "TREE" in giant caps, plates labeled "BASE" and "VARIANT", a stripe under the selected recipe.
options.case: Loses both axes: the quotation gag adds noise to every number, and stripes fight the graph.
options.kept: Every zone carries its literal label plate.
options.risk: Costume, not a system, on a data surface.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.lineage: surreal garden where rain falls by the color of its cloud
options.thesis: Recipes as habitats with their own gravity.
options.viewport: A garden field with recipes as habitats and rains as edges.
options.case: Loses both axes: bent baselines destroy tabular numerals, and the metaphor carries none of lineage.
options.kept: One dominant field per phone viewport.

options.label: Viewfinder Bracket HUD
options.thesis: The graph is the scene; readouts live in the corners.
options.viewport: Full-bleed graph with corner brackets and a tape-counter zoom bar.
options.case: Loses both axes: a HUD reads as camera, not kitchen, and segmented caps cannot set a method.
options.kept: Controls pinned to the corners; the center stays empty.
options.risk: Gimmick on every page but the tree.

options.label: HyperCard Shoebox
options.thesis: Every recipe is a card; buttons link cards; back retraces your trail.
options.viewport: A stack of fixed-proportion cards dissolving between each other.
options.case: Loses both axes: one-bit stipple kills a macro table at phone size, and cards-in-a-stack hide the DAG.

canonCard.label: The recipe app
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably: warm cream ground, serif titles, rounded cards, soft shadows.
canonCard.viewport: A card grid with a serif title, warm chips, and a soft-cornered detail panel — essentially the incumbent, at full polish.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every recipe app — and from what Batch already looks like.
